chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni (1) from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Khaybari from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qummi from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever visits the grave of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) - on the bank of the Euphrates - is like one who has visited God above His Throne."

key_terms.بِشَطِّ الْفُرَاتِ: on the bank of the Euphrates

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Rida on the Euphrates?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kulayni’s *Al-Kafi* (cited in *Tahdhib*) emphasizes the spiritual merit of visiting Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), though the phrase 'on the banks of the Euphrates' typically refers to Imam al-Husayn in Karbala, suggesting a possible textual variant or specific reference to al-Rida's shrine in Tus or a metaphorical connection. It equates the reward of this visitation to the exalted status of having visited God Himself above His Throne, emphasizing the unique proximity of the Imam to the Divine. This reflects the Shia concept of *Ziyarat* as a means of drawing near to Allah through the Imam, who serves as the perfect manifestation of Divine attributes.
